findings.statement: CA9 is a known target control with an ADC suitability of [gene=CA9; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.647]. Stomach, a vital organ, stains strongly while kidney does not stain. In the weakest quarter of donors the share of tumour cells expressing it is [gene=CA9; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_weakest_quarter_of_donors=24.3%], so heterogeneity limits a conjugate even though the score is good.

CD70 is among the top-ranked ADC candidates, with a suitability of [gene=CD70; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.746], and is a known target control. No normal-tissue staining data are available, so normal-tissue safety cannot be judged here. In the weakest quarter of donors [gene=CD70; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_weakest_quarter_of_donors=17.7%] of tumour cells express it.

SCARB1 (first in the target profile) has an ADC suitability of [gene=SCARB1; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.558]. Adrenal gland stains strongly and kidney stains at an intermediate level. Only [gene=SCARB1; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_weakest_quarter_of_donors=7.1%] of tumour cells express it in the weakest quarter of donors, so it is a weak conjugate candidate despite its tumour increase.

ENPP3, a known target control, has a suitability of [gene=ENPP3; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.578]. Kidney and duodenum both stain at the highest level, so on-target toxicity in normal tissue is a concern. In the weakest quarter of donors [gene=ENPP3; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_weakest_quarter_of_donors=21.3%] of tumour cells express it. A high score would not show that a conjugate works.

SLC16A3 is among the top three ADC candidates (suitability [gene=SLC16A3; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.725]) but is a multi-pass transporter with very few extracellular residues, which leaves little antibody-accessible surface. Adrenal gland stains strongly. In the weakest quarter of donors [gene=SLC16A3; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_weakest_quarter_of_donors=43.7%] of tumour cells express it, the most even expression among the genes checked.

CA9 is flagged as a subgroup target candidate for PBRM1 mutation. The mutant-minus-wild-type difference in CPTAC RNA is [gene=CA9; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; PBRM1.cptac_rna.mutant_minus_wildtype_log2=0.971], but the CPTAC protein adjusted p-value is [gene=CA9; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; PBRM1.cptac_protein.padj=0.067], so the flag is driven by RNA. It is lower in ccB than ccA in all three cohorts.

PSAT1 is not a subgroup target candidate for VHL, PBRM1, BAP1 or SETD2. Its BAP1 mutant-minus-wild-type difference in TCGA RNA is [gene=PSAT1; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; BAP1.tcga_rna.mutant_minus_wildtype_log2=1.711], but the CPTAC protein adjusted p-value is [gene=PSAT1; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; BAP1.cptac_protein.padj=0.396], so the protein level does not support it. It is higher in ccB than ccA.

PCK1 is not a subgroup target candidate for any of the four mutations. Its ccB-minus-ccA difference in TCGA RNA is [gene=PCK1; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; ccA_ccB.tcga_rna.ccB_minus_ccA_log2=-2.581], but in CPTAC protein it is [gene=PCK1; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; ccA_ccB.cptac_protein.ccB_minus_ccA_log2=0.017], so the RNA subtype signal is not seen at protein level.

In IMmotion150, higher CA9 expression is associated with longer benefit on sunitinib (log hazard ratio per SD [gene=CA9; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.sunitinib.log_hr_per_sd=-0.336], adjusted p-value [gene=CA9; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.sunitinib.padj=0.332]), which is not significant. The difference between arms has adjusted p-value [gene=CA9; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.difference_between_arms.padj=0.779], and no gene differs between arms after correction. These are leads, not predictions.

Higher PCK1 is associated with earlier progression on atezolizumab plus bevacizumab (log hazard ratio per SD [gene=PCK1; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.atezolizumab_bevacizumab.log_hr_per_sd=0.22], adjusted p-value [gene=PCK1; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.atezolizumab_bevacizumab.padj=0.572]). The difference between arms has adjusted p-value [gene=PCK1; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.difference_between_arms.padj=0.754], so no arm separation is shown.

NNMT has only the very small nivolumab trial result: log hazard ratio per SD [gene=NNMT; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.nivolumab_choueiri2016.log_hr_per_sd=0.34] (earlier progression with higher expression), adjusted p-value [gene=NNMT; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.nivolumab_choueiri2016.padj=0.782]. This is direction only and cannot support any treatment claim. No IMmotion150 arm is reported for this gene.

Higher PSAT1 is associated with earlier progression on atezolizumab (log hazard ratio per SD [gene=PSAT1; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.atezolizumab.log_hr_per_sd=0.164], adjusted p-value [gene=PSAT1; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.atezolizumab.padj=0.829]), which is not significant. Its biomarker value therefore rests on tumour data, not on trial response.

CD70 has an immune-cell share of tumour transcripts of [gene=CD70; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; immune_cell_share_of_tumour_transcripts=0.654], so part of its signal comes from immune cells. It correlates with CD8 T cells (Spearman rho [gene=CD70; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; rho_with_cd8_t_cells=0.278]). Its log hazard ratio on atezolizumab plus bevacizumab is [gene=CD70; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; log_hr_atezolizumab_bevacizumab=-0.383], a lead only.

FCGR3A is almost entirely immune-derived: its immune-cell share of tumour transcripts is [gene=FCGR3A; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; immune_cell_share_of_tumour_transcripts=0.999] and its Spearman rho with the immune score is [gene=FCGR3A; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; rho_with_immune_score=0.795]. Its rise in tumours reflects infiltration, not a tumour-cell target.

NNMT is not an immune gene: its immune-cell share of tumour transcripts is [gene=NNMT; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; immune_cell_share_of_tumour_transcripts=0.015] and its Spearman rho with CD8 T cells is [gene=NNMT; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; rho_with_cd8_t_cells=-0.127]. Its tumour increase therefore comes from tumour cells.

NNMT is attributed to RCC tumour cells in both Li 2022 and Zhang 2021 (same dominant group). The tumour-cell share is [gene=NNMT; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); li2022_tumour_cell_share=0.97] in Li 2022 and [gene=NNMT; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); zhang2021_tumour_cell_share=0.948] in Zhang 2021, so the cell attribution holds in a second dataset.

SCARB1 does not keep its cell-type call: the dominant group is Myeloid in Li 2022 and RCC in Zhang 2021. The tumour-cell share is [gene=SCARB1; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); li2022_tumour_cell_share=0.336] in Li 2022 versus [gene=SCARB1; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); zhang2021_tumour_cell_share=0.582] in Zhang 2021. Attribution to tumour cells is unresolved, which weakens it as a tumour-selective target.

CA9 is attributed to RCC tumour cells in both single-cell datasets, with tumour-cell shares of [gene=CA9; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); li2022_tumour_cell_share=0.976] in Li 2022 and [gene=CA9; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); zhang2021_tumour_cell_share=0.981] in Zhang 2021. The Zhang comparison rests on few paired donors.

SCARB1 protein replicates in the confirmatory CPTAC cohort: log2 fold change [gene=SCARB1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=2.334] with adjusted p-value [gene=SCARB1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_padj=3.28e-10]. Direction and significance agree with discovery.

NNMT protein replicates in the confirmatory cohort: log2 fold change [gene=NNMT; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=4.776] with adjusted p-value [gene=NNMT; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_padj=3.07e-46], the same up direction as discovery. Fold-change sizes differ because the technology differs.

PSAT1 protein is lower in tumours and replicates: log2 fold change [gene=PSAT1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=-3.946] with adjusted p-value [gene=PSAT1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_padj=9.71e-23]. Its single measured phosphosite does not replicate.

PCK1 protein is lower in tumours and replicates: log2 fold change [gene=PCK1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=-4.819] with adjusted p-value [gene=PCK1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_padj=3.53e-27]. Both measured phosphosites replicate.

HK2 protein does not replicate in the confirmatory cohort: the discovery increase (log2 fold change [gene=HK2; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_discovery_log2fc=2.106]) is not seen in the confirmatory data (log2 fold change [gene=HK2; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=-0.256], adjusted p-value [gene=HK2; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_padj=0.074]), which weakens its target-profile position.

caveats: Single-gene hits in IMmotion150 come from arms of about ninety patients; no gene differs between the two main arms after correction, so these are leads only.
A high ADC score does not show that a conjugate or radioligand would work. CD70 has no staining data, so its safety is unassessed.
EPAS1 was not profiled with the per-gene applied tools; PCK1 and PSAT1 are lower in tumours, so they are biomarkers, not ADC targets.
Subgroup flags rest on mutant vs wild-type comparisons with few mutant cases; the CA9 PBRM1 flag is RNA-driven.
Immune-cell-derived genes such as FCGR3A reflect infiltration, not tumour-cell expression.
